result.title: Decoding spatial and semantic information from large-scale visual cortical activity for natural-movie reconstruction
result.comment: 24 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables; 11-page supplementary information included as ancillary file
result.summary: Reconstructing natural visual experience from cortical population activity is a central challenge in neural decoding, particularly for calcium imaging, where signals are noisy, temporally filtered, and paired neural-video data are limited. Here we present Ca2REAL (Calcium Activity to Reconstruct Events, Appearance, and Layout), a neural-to-video framework that conditions a pretrained video diffusion model through separate layout and semantic controls derived from calcium activity. Using measured responses from 7,863 V1 neurons in one mouse, Ca2REAL reconstructed held-out natural-movie clips with 81.4% all-pairs stimulus-identification accuracy, with its clearest gains over deterministic baselines in perceptual and semantic measures. We further evaluated the framework in a stimulus-aligned virtual population of 116,705 neurons assembled from encoding-model-predicted responses across 11 independently recorded datasets. Perturbation and ablation analyses showed that reconstruction depends on distributed, stimulus-specific population structure, with layout and semantic pathways providing complementary spatial and identity information. Temporal analyses further showed improved preservation of semantic dynamics across reconstructed clips. These results show that large-scale cortical population activity constrains the spatial, semantic, and temporal structure of natural visual experience, providing a generative framework for high-fidelity neural reconstruction of dynamic visual scenes.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 Ca2REAL，用小鼠 V1 钙成像群体活动分别驱动预训练视频扩散模型的布局与语义控制通路，重建自然电影片段，并通过扰动与消融分析考察分布式群体结构及各通路的贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「布局—语义」分离通路与扰动/消融归因，可能为 LVR 中视觉细节与实体关系是否保留在内部状态、以及各因素的因果贡献如何拆分提供一种可借用的分析视角，需核查其指标能否迁移到模型 latent 评价。
